answer: Sybil resistance binds every identity to bonded collateral, so coordinated equivocation by k identities aggregates correlated evidence and imposes a quadratic penalty, O(k^2), rather than k independent fines. Detection also applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss for the controlled swarm, rapidly exhausting the operator’s escrow and deterring identity proliferation. A vertex cannot evade this exposure by shifting behind a horizon of aliases, while copper-like low-value accounts still inherit the group liability.
